sections.name: QueryProvider
sections.title: Query provider and cache settings
sections.what: Creates one cache for the page with fresh data for one minute, one retry on failure, and no refetch on window focus, then wraps the app in it along with the developer panel.
sections.why: Fewer repeated server calls make screens faster and reduce load. Refetch on focus is turned off, which is likely to avoid extra requests when users switch tabs.
sections.watch_out: The developer panel is always rendered here, so confirm it is removed or hidden in production.

summary: Wraps the web app in the data caching tool called TanStack Query, with settings for how long data stays fresh and how many retries happen.
purpose: Lets screens fetch server data once and reuse it, instead of asking the server again every time a screen opens. It also adds a developer panel for inspecting cached data.
why: The file header says production-grade caching strategy. Data is treated as fresh for one minute, and retries are kept low to avoid repeated slow calls.
how: Creates one query client when the provider first loads, sets the freshness time to one minute, sets one retry, and turns off refetching when the window regains focus. Wraps the children in the provider and adds the developer panel closed by default.
outputs: A context that lets child components fetch and cache server data.
risks: The developer panel is rendered without a check for production, so it may appear in live builds depending on how the library is set up. Cached health data stays in memory while the page is open.
debug: If data looks stale, check the one minute setting and whether a screen forces a refetch. If a request is retried unexpectedly, check the retry setting. If the developer panel appears in production, check the library's production rules.
